title: Use a translation responsibly
subtitle: Compare after your own structural reading, not instead of it.
overview: A translation can reveal options and alert you to missed structure, but it should not replace your observation of the Greek text.
Compare your map with a translation after a first pass. Ask what the translation has made explicit, smoothed, or left ambiguous.

sections.title: Comparison questions
rows: Does the translation preserve the clause relation?
Which Greek word supports its key English term?
What has English supplied for clarity?
Does the Greek permit another responsible wording?

items.grc: ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν.
items.en: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.

items.grc: ἐκείνου δεῖ αὐξάνειν, ἐμὲ δὲ ἐλαττοῦσθαι.
items.en: He must increase, but I must decrease.
